title.narrative: PERFORMANCE-BASED PARTNERSHIP SCHEME FOCUSING ON QUALITY PROGRAMMING, UNDERSTANDING CHANGE AND RESULTS FOR POOR HOUSEHOLDS AND COMMUNITIES

description.narrative: The A Healthy Future - Health and WASH System Strengthening and Community Action for Improved Child and Maternal Health and Nutrition programme will work in Centre-East Region, Kouritenga Province, Burkina Faso. It aims to contribute to Concern Burkina Faso’s Health, Nutrition and WASH thematic programme, and the goal of the grant is to improve maternal, neonatal and child health and nutritional status by improving access to quality essential services, household resilience and promoting sustainable behaviour change. The programme will support over 1,351,200 people living in extreme and poor households, including internally displaced people particular focus on women and children under five. This will be done through strengthened community health management committees that empower women and the extreme poor, tailored support and advocacy provided to address bottlenecks and gaps in delivery of essential child medical and nutrition supplies the 'last mile' to health facilities and increased health, nutrition sanitation and hygiene awareness and the reduction of adoption barriers facilitating sustainable behaviour change.. DRR 1: Through system strengthening, the programme is strengthening the resilience of the heath system. Capacity Building 1: Training and capacity building was provided to community volunteers on WASH and awareness raising campaigns were held on healt, nutrition and WASH topics. Gender Equality 2: this is the main objective of the outcome, which is aimed at as it focus on reducing barriers and increasing access of women to basic health and nutrition services. RMNC Health 1: The aim of this programme is to improve child and maternal health and nutritional status by improving access to essential health, nutrition, water, sanitation and hygiene services and by promoting sustainable behaviour change for optimal feeding, caring and hygiene for children under-five and their carers. The primary target groups are children under-five and women of reproductive age, particularly pregnant women. Nutrition 1: Improving the nutrition status of women and children through improved nutrition awareness among communities is a focus of this outcome.
